requirements.evidence: Contract implemented end to end: invokable signature and negative-priority guard in `app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:28-32`, locked inactive-queue re-check at `:54-58`, ticket-creation defaults at `:60-67`, and bounded collision retry at `:36-46`; `Ticket::nextCode`, `call` and the write-once guard at `app/Models/Ticket.php:78-89`, `:97-116`, `:31-46`; models, casts and relations at `app/Models/Queue.php:11-37` and `app/Models/Ticket.php:16-72`; `Entity::queues()` at `app/Models/Entity.php:46-49`; migrations, enums, exception and factories are present (`database/migrations/2026_10_29_044032_create_tickets_table.php:14-28`, `database/factories/TicketFactory.php:21-47`). Edge cases (A999/A1000, malformed codes, deletion gaps, stale-instance call) are covered by `tests/Feature/Ticket/NextCodeTest.php:51-83` and `tests/Feature/Ticket/CallTicketTest.php:85-95`.

conventions.evidence: Domain write lives in the action `app/Actions/IssueTicket.php`; call authorization goes through a policy/gate (`app/Policies/TicketPolicy.php:13-16`, `app/Models/Ticket.php:99`); migrations look artisan-generated and have reversible `down()` methods (`database/migrations/2026_10_29_044031_create_queues_table.php:30-33`, `database/migrations/2026_10_29_044032_create_tickets_table.php:34-37`); fillable and casts are deliberate (`app/Models/Queue.php:11`, `app/Models/Ticket.php:16`); docs and changelog are updated in the same change (`docs/business-rules.md:79-87`, `docs/database-schema.md:3,150,162`, `CHANGELOG.md:12`).

security.evidence: Call is authorized server-side before any write (`app/Models/Ticket.php:99`, `app/Policies/TicketPolicy.php:15`), and the unauthorized tests assert the ticket stays unchanged (`tests/Feature/Ticket/CallTicketTest.php:51-70`); priority and queue state are validated in the action (`app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:30-32`, `:54-58`); mass assignment is limited by `#[Fillable]` (`app/Models/Ticket.php:16`, `app/Models/Queue.php:11`); no Blade/user output, secrets or Livewire/HTTP code are involved.

tests.evidence: Pest tests cover issuance/defaults, negative priority, inactive and stale queues, retry bounds (`tests/Feature/Ticket/IssueTicketTest.php:18-129`), code allocation and its edge cases (`tests/Feature/Ticket/NextCodeTest.php:9-83`), write-once behavior (`tests/Feature/Ticket/TicketWriteOnceTest.php:11-58`), authorization and single/stale call (`tests/Feature/Ticket/CallTicketTest.php:24-95`), and queue/model/factory behavior (`tests/Feature/Queue/QueueTest.php:11-66`). Weak spots: the collision test at `IssueTicketTest.php:82-106` and the call-field test at `TicketWriteOnceTest.php:43-49`.

simplicity.evidence: One small action (`app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:17-77`) and a focused model API (`app/Models/Ticket.php:78-116`); `nextCode` is a single query chain (`:80-88`) rather than a new service or counter, and the factory reuses it (`database/factories/TicketFactory.php:37-39`). No repository/service layer or duplication; the only extra is the test-oriented `QueueFactory::inactive()` (`database/factories/QueueFactory.php:29-34`).

readability.evidence: Clear names and short methods; public behavior is documented (`app/Models/Ticket.php:74-96`, `app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:14-27`), and the write-once guard and call transaction have explanatory comments (`app/Models/Ticket.php:34-44`, `:101-115`). Style is consistent with the surrounding models; no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Only queue/ticket domain files are added or touched: migrations, models, enums, exception, action, policy, factories, tests, docs and `CHANGELOG.md`; no unrelated refactors or out-of-scope features (no HTTP, Livewire, totem or call-next selection).

issues.explanation: The competing issuance is inserted with a raw insert inside the action's own transaction, so it is rolled back on the unique violation; the retry recomputes A001 and the test asserts A001. It never shows a committed collision advancing the code to A002, and it would also pass with a retry implementation that reused the same code.

The test claims the call fields may change but asserts only `status`; `called_at` and `called_by_user_id` are absent from the Ticket fillable list (`app/Models/Ticket.php:16`), so this `update()` silently drops them and the assertion passes without proving they can change.

The docs state that deleting the most recent valid ticket frees its number again, which is the natural result of the last-code approach but contradicts the task's unqualified 'deleting a ticket does not reuse its number'. Confirm the intended rule; if reuse is forbidden, `nextCode` needs persisted sequence state rather than only existing rows.

review.summary: Adds the queue/ticket persistence core: migrations, models and casts, enums, the inactive-queue exception, the IssueTicket action with locked state checks and collision retry, nextCode/call with write-once and single-call guards, a TicketPolicy, factories, docs and a broad Pest suite. The contract and edge cases are covered and the code is clean and secure; the main gaps are two weak tests (the collision test does not simulate a committed conflict, and the call-field test does not assert the two non-fillable fields) and a documentation ambiguity about reusing the latest deleted number, so this is an approve-with-minor-fixes.
